A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perturbation Forgery study and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. v3 includes an appendix; v4 ends at the references despite pointing to supplementary material. The comparison concerns content actually included in these supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v3 reports original detection experiments on ImageNet100, facial datasets and CIFAR-10, together with ablations, sensitivity analyses and inference timings.

after.justification: v4 retains original detection results and reports additional adaptive-attack, detector-aware attack, initialization and estimation-sample-size experiments.

M1.justification: The Gaussian noise-distribution perturbation, saliency/GradCAM/Sobel masks, pseudo-adversarial sample generation and binary cross-entropy training remain unchanged. The equations and Algorithm 1 describe the same procedure; revised wording and equation references do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: All five datasets remain represented; CIFAR-10 already appeared in v3's appendix. v4 substantially extends threat-scenario coverage with explicitly detector-aware white-box attacks on CIFAR-10. ImageNet100 testing also adds BPDA+EOT and MM while dropping RFGSM, VNIM and SNIM. Generative and facial attack coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The detector comparator sets in the ImageNet100 and facial comparisons remain unchanged. However, v3's appendix Table 7 compares against SPAD and EPSAD on CIFAR-10, whereas v4's CIFAR-10 analyses report only the proposed detector. Comparator coverage is therefore reduced on that dataset.

E3.justification: v4 introduces joint classifier–detector attacks with weight alpha=1, a six-attack initialization grid and estimation sizes from 100 to 2000. For retained ImageNet100 evaluation, v3 says attacks are seen by LID; v4 says they are unseen by every detector and explicitly describes detector-blind gray-box generation. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing reruns. AUC and AUROC denote the same metric.

E4.justification: v4 adds detector-aware robustness, initial-attack dependence and estimation-sample-size analyses. It omits v3's appendix sweeps of distribution/mask parameters and training-versus-testing attack intensity, plus the CIFAR-10 t-SNE analysis. The mask-component ablation and ImageNet100 t-SNE analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Random sampling used by the method does not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 newly reports proposed-method AUROCs of 0.9927 for BPDA+EOT and 0.9944 for MM, white-box scores of 0.9019–0.9180, and initialization/sample-size findings. v3's CIFAR-10 comparative table and appendix sensitivity results are absent. Shared entries in Tables 2–5 and inference timings remain numerically unchanged. The new attack settings do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v4 retains Definition 1, Theorem 1 and the open-covering discussion, but no longer includes v3's appendix proofs, explicit Wasserstein bounds and Corollary 1 proof. Its reference to supplementary material provides no replacement derivation within the supplied PDF, substantially reducing the included theoretical development.

C1.justification: The proximity/open-covering argument and Perturbation Forgery contributions remain central. The abstract's rationale, introduction and conclusion soften several claims from detecting 'all types' to 'various types' of unseen attacks. This is a limited qualification; the abstract still claims detection of any unseen attack within the listed families.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations linking white-box robustness to open covering, asserting initial-attack independence and identifying insufficient estimation data as a failure condition. v3's explanations of attack-intensity mismatch, extreme mask thresholds and difficult scale-parameter tuning are absent. v4 refers limitations to supplementary material that is not included.

D1.justification: v4 retains basic detector hyperparameters and the paper's code link, and adds a general ten-step/step-size-two attack description. However, it omits v3's optimizer and hardware specifications, preprocessing instructions, victim-model and generator configurations, baseline implementation links, and practical 32×32 noise construction. These are losses of documentation, not established implementation changes.

R1.justification: v4 adds literature on detector evasion and adaptive robustness, including Carlini and Wagner, Bryniarski et al., Tramer, Gao et al. and Hill et al., and explicitly discusses adaptive attacks. References supporting removed attack variants and implementation details disappear. The broad positioning against adversarial, synthetic-image and face-forgery detectors remains.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, paragraphs are polished, AUC becomes AUROC, and numbered sections and finer analysis subsections are introduced. The central exposition and main section order remain substantially intact; most retained material receives editorial refinement rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned to display existing detection scores and timings, absorbing v3's separate timing table. Figure 2 is relabeled and restyled. v3's appendix Figures 4–7 and CIFAR-10 comparison table disappear, while v4 introduces an initialization heatmap and white-box/sample-size tables. Figures, tables and their page placement are substantially reorganized.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical scrutiny through adaptive and detector-aware evaluations and initialization/sample-size studies. However, the supplied PDF loses theorem proofs, important reproducibility details, attack-intensity sensitivity evidence and explicit tuning limitations while retaining most headline results. These substantial opposing effects, compounded by references to supplementary material absent from v4.pdf, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
